text: [serious, cinematic storyteller, brisk pace] The libraries closed on a Monday. By Friday, no one remembered why they had been open. The old teachers grew quiet. One by one, they died. And no one took their place. Children learned chants instead of letters. Parents stopped asking questions they couldn't answer. And on the hill outside the city, something old was uncovered. A stone figure, buried for centuries. At first, people only came to look. Then they brought flowers. Then they began to walk around it… slowly… in circles. No one told them to. It just felt right. The Prophet said that before the Hour, knowledge would be taken away, ignorance would spread, and some would return to the idols of old. That spring, the rain came early. The harvest was the biggest anyone had ever seen. And with it came more money than anyone knew what to do with.
